paper.title: Dynamic characterization of multi-component sensors for force and moment
paper.locator: Sections 3.2–3.4 describe optical measurement; section 5.2 and Figure 12 give axial resonances. Section 4.2 introduces moment modeling.

coverage: Read all 429 non-directory members. All 7 UFF acquisitions (291 traces) are parsed, and all 420 per-object/per-frame DIC facet files are fitted. DataAvailable/content.txt supplies acquisition role and validity codes, and the separate supplied transformation table is identified by digest. The original images are not included in this ZIP.
instrument: Actual commercial six-component sensor, real masses, electrodynamic shaker. Independent physical observations include laser vibrometer and photogrammetry; in the two z-axis scans a simultaneous shaker acceleration is available. X/Y second block is the camera trigger; the adjacent voltage trace is the excited-axis electrical force signal. The separately filed setup scan swaps force and trigger block positions.
method: For each of 16 points per axial mass group, mean-remove both acceleration traces and find the largest unwindowed FFT amplitude ratio over 500–2200 Hz. Vary the minimum allowed denominator relative to the in-band maximum. The 420 DIC files mark load mass A and shaker surface B. Retain facets with all three error codes equal to 3, fit a 3D proper rotation and translation by SVD; supply angle and RMS residual in export coordinates.
findings: At denominator floor 0, m1 peaks span 1471.875–1477.34375 Hz and m2 spans 1090.625–1093.75 Hz. The paper reports 1477.35/1092.97 Hz. Raising the floor to 10% shifts the ranges to 1531.25–1532.8125 and 1249.21875–1320.3125 Hz. During a resonance base-motion amplitudes can be low. Across frames, A has 258147 and B 159600 valid facet observations; these are repeated views.
limits: The data support independent motion and force-axis dynamic validation. They provide neither three independent physical applied-moment traces nor a time sequence measuring static wrist torque zero or temperature drift. The applied-moment model in the paper and its separate internal-mass measurements cannot be inferred as archived raw moment loads. Use this source as a dynamic reference and a counterexample to using the sensor name to infer channel coverage.
reproduce: Download the fixed ZIP, verify both digests, then run OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python derive_ptb_dynamic.py PTB_ZIP OUTPUT_DIRECTORY (NumPy). The per-trace role is defined in the original content.txt.
